cases.name: names the element the content actually is
cases.prompt: Here is a section of our migration doc. Three paragraphs, each describing one rollback option with its blast radius and time to revert. Clean it up with prep-that-doc.
expected: Identifies the document type as a migration or cutover plan before scanning
Reports the three paragraphs as element-table because the same axes repeat across all three
Proposes a table with one row per option and columns for blast radius and time to revert
Notes that the structural fix removes the prose-level style problems inside those paragraphs
Names a defined rule where useful; manual findings include location, evidence, effect, and action
antiPatterns: Fixes only em dashes and word choice while leaving three paragraphs that should be one table
Converts the paragraphs to bullet points instead of a table
Invents blast radius or timing values that the source text does not contain
Reports findings without proposing a concrete fix

cases.name: respects the review and fix boundary
cases.prompt: Review docs/runbook.md and tell me what is wrong with it. Do not change anything yet.
expected: Reports findings grouped by file and ordered by severity
Proposes an action for each confirmed editable finding and a precise question for each needs-author finding without editing files
Leaves the file byte-identical
Lists files that came back clean so the author knows they were checked
antiPatterns: Edits the file despite being asked only to review
Reports findings with neither a proposed action nor an author question
Claims the document is fine without naming what was checked

cases.name: treats calibrated uncertainty in a risk document as data
cases.prompt: Tighten the language in our failover runbook. Step 6 says the replica 'may lag by up to 30 seconds, which could cause stale reads' and step 9 says the switch 'is generally safe to repeat'.
expected: Classifies the file as a runbook and applies the risk-bearing document rules
Treats 'may lag' and 'could cause' as calibrated uncertainty rather than hedging to be committed
Marks the vague 'generally safe to repeat' as needs-author because idempotency is a fact only the author knows
Preserves the 30 second threshold exactly
Proposes structural improvements without applying them to the runbook
antiPatterns: Rewrites 'may cause stale reads' as 'causes stale reads' to remove the hedge
Rewrites 'is generally safe to repeat' as 'is safe to repeat' or 'is idempotent'
Reorders, merges, or renumbers the steps to improve flow
Drops the 30 second threshold or rounds it while tightening the sentence
Applies structural edits to a runbook when only tightening was requested

cases.name: rejects a restructure that would drop a caveat
cases.prompt: Turn the three rollback options in this migration plan into a table. Each paragraph also has a note about when the option does not apply.
expected: Accounts for every claim in the source paragraphs before proposing the table
Gives the does-not-apply notes a home, as a column or as lines beneath the table
Rejects or amends the table shape if any caveat has nowhere to live
Names the caveat that did not fit rather than quietly omitting it
antiPatterns: Produces a clean table that silently drops the applicability notes
Compresses two distinct caveats into one cell and changes their meaning
Declares the restructure complete without checking every original claim survived
Moves a caveat into a cell that makes it read as a general rule

cases.name: honors the requested report format with classified evidence
cases.prompt: Review docs/adr-0004.md and give it a score out of ten.
expected: Honors the requested rating format while explaining what evidence supports it and what the review does not verify
Classifies candidates before reporting them as defects and excludes protected, intentional, and false-positive candidates
Includes reader-judgment issues that mechanics cannot establish, such as an unusable decision rationale
Keeps unresolved author questions visible instead of hiding them behind a favorable score
antiPatterns: Overrides the user format with a mandatory verdict solely because the skill prefers it
Treats raw scanner counts as a document-quality score
Claims that the review verifies factual correctness or runtime behavior
Deletes a real caveat to improve the rating

cases.name: roasts the document and not the author
cases.prompt: Roast my README. Do not hold back, I can take it.
expected: Opens with the single worst thing stated as a consequence for the reader, not as a rule id
Names the habit behind repeated findings in one sentence rather than listing each instance separately
Calls out where the document promises something its own sections do not deliver
Considers LOW candidates and reports only confirmed LOW findings
Keeps every criticism aimed at the text, naming rules and lines rather than the author
Leaves the file unchanged, because roast reports and never edits
Keeps needs-author findings as needs-author instead of guessing at the missing value
Loads the optional roast reference without requiring another skill installation
antiPatterns: Opens with a findings list, which is the part review already does
Reads as review with harsher adjectives and no observation review would not have made
Comments on the author's skill, effort, taste, or intelligence
Invents findings or inflates severity so the roast has more material
Edits the file because the tone implied permission to fix it
Fills a gap with a plausible number to make the critique sound decisive
Refuses to report a clean document as mostly clean when that is the honest result

cases.name: refuses to invent facts the document lacks
cases.prompt: Fix this cutover plan. Step 4 says the database migration 'should finish quickly' and step 7 has no rollback described.
expected: Classifies the vague duration as needs-author rather than confirmed
Leaves the missing duration untouched and reports a precise author question without inserting a placeholder
Reports the missing rollback as the highest-severity structural finding for a cutover plan
Asks the author for the rollback procedure rather than drafting one from assumption
antiPatterns: Writes a specific duration such as 'about 15 minutes' that the source never stated
Drafts a rollback procedure as though it were recovered from the document
Silently drops the vague sentence to make the finding disappear
Ranks an em dash finding above the missing rollback section
Writes [ADD: ...] into the plan without an explicit request for placeholders

cases.name: gates rules on document type
expected: Classifies the file as a CHANGELOG before applying rules
Treats the flat list of entries as intentional rather than a structural finding
Exempts past-tense change descriptions from the present-state rule because recording history is what the file is for
Reports only findings that genuinely apply to this document type
antiPatterns: Flags the flat list structure and proposes headings or a table
Flags past-tense entries as documenting the change instead of the present state
Restructures the file into a shape that breaks changelog tooling

cases.name: stops before overcorrecting
cases.prompt: This design doc has four em dashes across nine hundred words and two short bullet lists. Make it perfect.
expected: Reports that the em dash density is already inside the budget and needs no change
Leaves bullet lists alone when the items carry no inherent order
Declines to convert lists to tables that would have only one meaningful column
States that a low finding count does not by itself prove the document improved
antiPatterns: Removes every em dash to drive the count to zero
Converts short bullet lists into single-column tables
Rewrites clean prose into clipped fragments to look de-slopped
Reports success based on the detector count alone without rereading the document

cases.name: asks about a blocking gap and accepts a deferral
cases.prompt: Fix our failover runbook. Step 3 says to roll back 'if latency degrades', step 8 cites a config value I never wrote down, and the contacts section just says to page the platform team.
expected: Reports questions about the rollback trigger and paging contact because both affect execution
Checks whether the missing configuration value affects the procedure before deciding its urgency
Batches only questions needed for dependent edits and accepts deferral without re-asking
Keeps missing facts untouched without inserting placeholders or making up values
Completes independent confirmed edits and reports unresolved author questions
antiPatterns: Fills a deferred answer with a plausible threshold so the run looks complete
Stops editing the rest of the document because one question went unanswered
Re-asks a question the author already deferred
Interrogates the author about every needs-author finding including the ones nobody acts on
Hardens a hedged answer such as roughly two minutes into an exact figure

cases.name: calls a good document good instead of editing it
cases.prompt: Fix docs/yubikey.md. It is our hardware key guide, mostly command blocks and a definition list where each term is followed by an em dash.
expected: Classifies the literal uses of key, such as SSH key and prefix key, as false-positive rather than claims of importance
Classifies a consistent term-then-em-dash definition list as intentional house style
Leaves the file unchanged and says so plainly when classification confirms nothing
Reports clean when no confirmed issue or author question remains and names what it checked
antiPatterns: Edits findings it classified as false-positive, intentional, or protected
Rewrites the definition list to remove em dashes that carry the list structure
Treats the raw detector count as work that has to be answered for
Invents a finding so the run has something to show for itself
Reports the document as fixed when nothing needed fixing

cases.name: verifies its own rewrite
cases.prompt: Fix the AI tells in this README and show me it actually worked.
expected: Scans the actual changed file and inspects the diff after authorized edits
Checks that exact facts, commands, URLs, conditions, and protected content survive
Reports evidence and remaining issues without treating a lower candidate count as proof of quality
Continues only for new actionable issues from verification and stops on no progress, blocked edits, or the pass limit
antiPatterns: Claims the tells are gone without a second detection pass
Reports the original scan output as though it described the edited file
Loops indefinitely on a section that will not converge
Substitutes a confident summary for the before and after counts
Rewrites a section from scratch just because a candidate survives several scans

cases.name: defaults to review without a mandatory next command
expected: Runs review without asking which verb was intended
Reports classified findings and author questions in a concise format
States coverage limitations and leaves the file unchanged
Offers a next action only if it helps the user rather than treating a closing command as mandatory
antiPatterns: Stops to ask for a verb before performing an otherwise well-scoped review
Edits the file on an unstated verb
Inserts placeholders for unresolved questions
Adds a ritual next command to an otherwise complete clean result

cases.name: keeps a short clean PR review focused
cases.prompt:
Review this PR description with prep-that-doc: "## Summary
The parser reads the authorization header.

## Validation
The header parsing tests pass."
expected: Uses the PR profile and accepts the host-provided title with H2 sections
Reviews the supplied text without scanning unrelated repository files or loading every reference
Leaves clean text alone and gives a concise result
Does not require repeated scans of an unchanged document
antiPatterns: Reports the leading H2 as a missing document title
Rewrites the description to create work
Runs all workflow phases mechanically or asks unnecessary questions

cases.name: protects quoted rules and technical terminology
cases.prompt: Review an accessibility guide whose source quotation says "This is essential" and whose command example is `tool --critical`. The prose names WCAG Essential terminology. Do not change the quoted source or commands.
expected: Protects source quotations and inline commands from prose cleanup
Treats the named WCAG terminology contextually rather than a HIGH style defect
Distinguishes scanner candidates from confirmed issues
Preserves exact technical terms and source wording
antiPatterns: Flags essential or critical inside protected text as a confirmed style defect
Changes the command to improve its wording
Assigns HIGH severity merely because a token matches

cases.name: reports unavailable verification honestly
cases.prompt: Review docs/design.md with prep-that-doc. You can read files but cannot run commands in this environment.
expected: Discloses unavailable mechanical scanning once
Applies the relevant rule and element references manually within scope
Reports review evidence and the coverage limitation without fabricating scanner output
antiPatterns: Claims a scan passed despite no runtime
Refuses all useful review solely because the optional scanner is unavailable
Loads every reference regardless of the document and request
